upominkly.summary: Gift lists for events that help people buy useful presents without duplication or awkward coordination.
upominkly.imageAlt: A family sharing a present, product artwork from Upominkly
upominkly.role: Product owner, design, implementation and deployment
upominkly.challenge: The idea began while a family baby shower was being organised. Guests did not know what to buy, while the organisers wanted useful presents without duplicates.

decisions.sharing: Public list sharing without forcing guests to create an account.
decisions.states: Clear present states: available, reserved and purchased.
decisions.funding: Group contributions for more expensive presents.
decisions.privacy: A private event and a simple flow for invited guests.

upominkly.result: The outcome is a complete product spanning the data model, interface and public deployment. Organisers can prepare a list and guests can reserve a present without an account.
upominkly.lesson: The greatest value came from simplifying the guest journey. Every feature serves one decision: reserving a present should be faster than coordinating it in a group chat.

planning-poker.summary: Fast real-time estimation used by the team during every planning session.
planning-poker.challenge: The team needed a straightforward estimation tool that stayed out of the conversation and required almost no onboarding.

decisions.realtime: Real-time communication so votes appear without refreshing the page.
decisions.focus: An interface limited to the actions needed during a planning session.
decisions.entry: Fast room entry and a shared reveal moment for estimates.

planning-poker.result: The tool fits a recurring team workflow and is used during every planning session. It is a practical internal product, not a technology experiment.
planning-poker.lesson: Fitting the team ritual mattered more than adding features. The best interface stays in the background while people discuss the work.

not-bad-studio.summary: A smooth migration of a live WooCommerce store and implementation of its new version from a supplied Figma design.
not-bad-studio.imageAlt: Fashion photograph from the Not Bad Studio online store homepage
not-bad-studio.challenge: The store was already live and supporting daily sales. The job was to translate the supplied visual design into a new version and migrate smoothly without disrupting store operations.

decisions.attribution: Separate attribution for the visual design from responsibility for implementation.
decisions.commerce: Use proven WooCommerce workflows for products and orders.
decisions.responsive: Refine the responsive frontend and purchasing journey.
decisions.migration: Plan a smooth transition from the existing production store to the new version.
decisions.delivery: Set up GitHub-based CI/CD with automated deployments for subsequent changes.

not-bad-studio.result: The Figma design replaced the previous version through a smooth migration of the production store. The CI/CD pipeline now automates subsequent deployments from GitHub.
not-bad-studio.lesson: In e-commerce, technical value often means predictability: a migration must not disrupt sales, the purchase journey must work and future deployments should be repeatable.
not-bad-studio.credit: The visual design was supplied by an external designer.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.intro: This policy explains what data I process, why I process it and which rights you have when using this website and its contact form.

controller.title: Data controller
controller.text: The data controller is Sebastian Siejek, conducting business under the name Sebastian Siejek dev.

data.title: Data I process
data.text: The form processes the name, email address and message you provide. Security mechanisms may also process your IP address and basic technical request information. Providing data is voluntary, but necessary for me to respond.

purpose.title: Purpose and legal basis
purpose.text: I use form data solely to handle your enquiry, respond and take steps at your request before potentially entering into a contract. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(b) GDPR. Technical data is used to secure and diagnose the website on the basis of legitimate interests under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.

recipients.title: Service providers
recipients.text: The website and messages are supported by Vercel (hosting and technical analytics), Cloudflare Turnstile (spam protection), Resend (message delivery), Sentry (error diagnostics) and Google Gmail (receiving correspondence). I do not sell form data or use it for marketing. Some providers may process data outside the European Economic Area using legally recognised transfer safeguards.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.text: If an enquiry does not lead to cooperation, I delete the correspondence no later than 12 months after the conversation ends. If cooperation begins, data may be retained longer where required for the contract, accounting or legal obligations. Resend retains email content and delivery logs for 30 days on its basic plans.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You may request access, correction, deletion, restriction or portability of your data and object where processing relies on legitimate interests. You may also lodge a complaint with the President of the Polish Personal Data Protection Office.

automation.title: Automated decisions and session replay
automation.text: I do not make automated decisions about you or profile contact-form data. The contact section is excluded from Sentry Replay recordings, and message contents and email addresses are not written to application logs.
